# Workbook mapping `imprint-xlsx-spike-1`

**Status:** spike output (SP-05). Generated by `gen-mapping.mjs` from `mapping.mjs`. Synthetic data only.

This is the documented mapping OpenSCG spec §10.4 asks for. OpenSCG 0.1 defines no workbook layout, so this one is ours. It is **not** a DoD or DTIC layout.

## Statement printed in every workbook

> GENERIC EXPORT — NOT A DTIC SUBMISSION. This workbook is a documented mapping of an OpenSCG guide, produced by an experimental Imprint spike. It has not been checked against any DoD or DTIC template and must not be described as meeting DoDM 5200.45 or any submission format. The OpenSCG JSON file is the authoritative copy; see the loss report for what this workbook does not carry. The digest shown identifies the signed JSON payload; it does not prove this workbook matches it.

## Rules that apply to every sheet

- **Rows 1–3 of every sheet** repeat the document banner (`document_markings.banner`), the labels `SYNTHETIC` (when `synthetic` is true) and `DRAFT / NOT APPROVED` (unless the revision has a technically valid attestation), and the guide ID, revision ID and payload digest (spec §10.1).
- **Print header and footer** repeat the banner, centred, on every printed page. The footer also carries the labels and page numbers.
- **Row 6 is the header row.** It is frozen and has a filter. Data starts on row 7.
- **Every value is a text cell.** No formulas, no Excel dates, no numbers. Dates stay as `YYYY-MM-DD` text, so no time-zone shift. Cells use the Text number format (`@`) so they stay text if someone edits them.
- **Formula injection.** Text that starts with `=`, `+`, `-`, `@`, tab or CR is stored as a shared string (`t="s"`), never as a formula (spec §10.4). It is not altered (no leading apostrophe), so the round trip is exact.
- **Characters XML cannot hold** (CR, other control characters) and literal `_xHHHH_` sequences are escaped the OOXML way (`_x000D_`, `_x005F_`). Excel and LibreOffice decode these.
- **Lists** (references, §1.4 categories, document controls) put one item per line in one cell.
- **Display-only columns** are written for people (for example "Level: U to C (see conditions)") and ignored when the workbook is read back.
- **Bytes are deterministic** for a given guide and export time: every zip entry gets the same timestamp.

## Sheet `Links`

Related guides, earlier revisions, recorded events and review evidence.

| Column | JSON pointer (relative to the row's item) | Encoding |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Relation | #rel (row bookkeeping) | text |
| Guide ID | `/guide_id` | text |
| Revision ID | `/revision_id` | text |
| Title | `/title` | text |
| Kind | `/kind` | text |
| Reference | `/reference` | text |
| Date | `/date` | text |
| URI | `/uri` | text |
| Payload digest (SHA-256) | `/payload_digest/value` | text |
| Note | `/note` | text |

Row bookkeeping columns: `#order` is the entry's position in `/entries` (elements and compilations are on separate sheets, so this keeps the original order); `#entry` links a control or source to its entry; `#rel` says which list a Links row came from (`supersedes`, `superseded_by`, `previous_revision`, `event`, `review_evidence`).

## Sheet `Mapping`

The workbook repeats this table, so a reader holding only the workbook can see where each column comes from.

## Deliberately not carried

| Pointer | Why |
| --- | --- |
| `/extensions` | Extension data can be any JSON and may be must-understand. It stays in the JSON only; the loss report lists it. |
| `/entries[]/extensions` | Same as guide-level extensions. |
| `/attestations` | Signatures are binary and travel as the detached attestation next to the workbook, not inside it. |

Everything else in the OpenSCG 0.1 schema is carried. `out/coverage.md` proves that field by field with a round trip.
